question: At Euclid High School, the number of students taking the AMC \(10\) was \(60\) in \(2002,\) \(66\) in \(2003,\) \(70\) in \(2004,\) \(76\) in \(2005,\) \(78\) in \(2006,\) and is \(85\) in \(2007.\) Between what two consecutive years was there the largest percentage increase?
solution:
A percentage increase compares the added students with the earlier year's count. From \(2002\) to \(2003\), the increase was
\[
\frac{66-60}{60}=\frac{1}{10}=10\%.
\]
For the four later intervals, the increases were respectively \(4,6,2,7\) students. Each was less than \(10\%\) of its starting count:
\[
\begin{aligned}
4&<0.1(66)=6.6,\\
6&<0.1(70)=7,\\
2&<0.1(76)=7.6,\\
7&<0.1(78)=7.8.
\end{aligned}
\]
Thus all four later percentage increases were below \(10\%\). The largest occurred between \(\boxed{2002\text{ and }2003}\), choice A.
